thread.title: Not So High On Skyworks - Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS)

author: Old School Value
title: Not So High On Skyworks - Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS)

organizations.name: wall st. ignored signs of trouble for months

text:
Editor's note: Seeking Alpha is proud to welcome Old School Value as a new contributor. It's easy to become a Seeking Alpha contributor and earn money for your best investment ideas. Active contributors also get free access to the SA PRO archive. Click here to find out more »
Story Time The market has been pretty wild lately.
I woke up to a New York Times news alert and lead story Monday, " Wall St. Ignored Signs of Trouble for Months. Now It Sees Risks Everywhere ." Trade wars, the Fed, new Trump allegations, the Huawei CFO arrest, the business cycle, Oh My! If there were one piece that tried to pull in as many narratives as possible to explain the recent volatility, this was it.
These factors may or may not be causal, so when journalists start doing this, I call it "Story Time." (I got this from Kaiser Fung , a data scientist.) It's when people shift from an evidence-based examination of facts to a speculative explanation. It's human nature to want to understand things, but we have to be careful about how we extrapolate from data.
The Skyworks Narrative One company we've been asked about a few times in the last couple of days is Skyworks ( SWKS ) , a manufacturer of semiconductor for Internet of Things (IoT) devices and mobile phones. It hit the top of Gurufocus' Buffett-Munger screener this week and is all over Seeking Alpha.
One look at its price, and you can see why:
Source: Google Finance
It's off more than 40% from its 2018 high in March, and that's compared to a drop of only around 7.6% for the S&P 500 over the same time frame.
Its fall began in mid-March after Trump signed the memo to apply tariffs on $50B of goods from China. Unfortunately for Skyworks, about 80% of its revenue comes from China. Similarly-exposed semiconductor manufacturers, like Qualcomm ( QCOM ) and Qorvo ( QRVO ), followed a very similar trajectory, initially.
Source: Yahoo Finance
But then things got worse for Skyworks. It reported Q3 earnings on July 19, which were a beat and resulted in an initial pop, but gave it all back plus another 5% the next day. It chugged slowly down vs. the S&P until its Q4 earnings, where it dropped another 12.5% over the following 4 days.
So what's been going on the last two quarters?
Quality, Value, and Growth Metrics From a quality perspective, things still look pretty good. The business is generating solid FCF on its sales and its Cash Return on Invested Capital (CROIC) is above 20%. Those metrics have deteriorated of late, but this looks more like normal variance than a major problem. For being a cost-competitive supplier, its margins are pretty impressive. It's a solid B in terms of Quality:
Source: Old School Value
It's beginning to look cheap, too. Its Value Score has increased quite a bit of late. Pretty much all of the key value metrics are at 5- and 10-year lows, from P/E to EV/EBIT or EBITDA. In the below chart, red just means the metric has gone down, so in this case, it means it's getting cheaper.
Source: Old School Value
My major hang-up with this company is its growth. Its 2018 fiscal year ended in September, with annual revenue growth of 5.9%. This masks the comparable quarterly growth trends, however, which were down in Q3 and only up 2.3% in Q4:
Source: Self, using Edgar Online data exported from Old School Value
I suspect analysts have their own version of this chart and this was a key factor in its price plunges after Q3 and Q4.
The Longer-term Case to Buy From the chart, you can clearly see some cyclicality. The company is product-driven and rises and falls based on new launches and new technologies. It announced a bunch of new stuff in Q4, so maybe we're in that cyclical trough and things will go up.
Proponents of buying SWKS's current dip point to its products in the 5G space, plus recent announcements from US carriers that suggest they are speeding up their rollouts of this next-gen technology. Skyworks supplies both Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) so will benefit from the incorporation of 5G technology in a huge number of mobile phone units.
It also has a strong presence in the IoT space, with products in connected cars, smart speakers, and smart lighting. Customers include Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet's Nest ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Hyundai. It recently closed a $425M acquisition to buy Avnera Corp, which has electronic circuit audio signal processing expertise that should aid it in many voice-activated applications.
We know both of these markets will grow over time, probably quite substantially. What's less clear is what Skyworks' position will be, and what its journey will look like.
Near-term Troubles At the same time, 47% of its revenue in 2018 was from Apple, which is having its own growth issues, especially with respect to units, which is what matters for SWKS. Even if you believe Apple's growth will get sparked by new services, or by price increases, SWKS will not share in either of those, as it is paid on volume.
To make matters worse, Apple has made it clear that 5G won't be introduced into its phones until 2020. This may be justified based on carrier rollouts, but it sure doesn't help Skyworks.
When almost half your revenue looks to be flat or down for the foreseeable future, it's hard to find a reason to buy.
IoT may be an important future revenue diversifier for SWKS, but it doesn't appear that management believes it will make much of a difference in the short term.
Skyworks' revenue guidance for Q1 is $1.02B, which would be a 3% decline from the $1.05B it posted 2018Q1. Its own management doesn't think its initiatives are enough to grow right now.
Throw in the uncertainty around China, where Skyworks has outsized exposure, and the company could be set for a painful short to medium term.
Valuing Skyworks in the Face of Uncertainty The problem is, we don't know. We can tell ourselves stories, but we'd be extrapolating beyond what the data tell us. We can see the fundamentals eroding, and we can tell stories about why that will or will not continue, but I think for now we should take the current situation at face value.
So, what is a fair FCF/Owner Earnings growth to use in our valuation? Well, over the last few years, its top-line growth has averaged around 6%. It was higher before, but I don't know that things can go back to that. Prices on current generation products have declined, and the next generation won't be here for a while. SWKS's earnings, FCF, and Owner Earnings have all been growing much faster, but it's hard to see how this is sustainable without more revenue growth, especially in the face of a rapidly weakening global economy. We can tell a story about scale, but even that has its limits.
If I plug in a moderate Owner Earnings growth rate (5%) into my DCF valuation, with a healthy discount rate due to the uncertainty (12%), SWKS's price is right at its fair value.
Source: Old School Value
But, it wouldn't take much to make this look good if you believed in higher future growth.
One other factor that is worth emphasizing is that this company has a solid balance sheet. No debt, strong quick and current ratios, and as mentioned before, strong cash flow generation. This is a company that will be able to weather a few storms.
Conclusion So, what does this mean? Well, it really depends on whether you want to tell yourself stories about the future growth of IoT, 5G, and SWKS's competitive position within these obviously-growing markets. Or as an acquisition target within semiconductors, which is (was?) about as hot for M&A as it gets. I don't have specific insight or expertise here, so I'm not willing to prognosticate. I would call this more of a growth play that's currently at a decent value if you have a long enough time frame and are willing to go to Story Time.
There are a lot of other better-valued companies out there right now with less uncertainty. But if you want a piece of tech action, this might not be a bad place to play.
And, as you might expect, there are a lot of people that are pretty positive on SWKS if you search this site. I encourage you to read people making the case for the stock. Just ask yourself, are they speculating or drawing sound conclusions from the facts?
